headline: Mistral preprint reports small time-series models leading three forecasting benchmarks
summary: An October 27 arXiv report describes Timestral, four probabilistic time-series forecasting models from 5M to 209M parameters. The authors report that Timestral-209M ranks first on six aggregate metrics across GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench, with smaller variants on the reported size–accuracy Pareto front. The method separates forecast tokens from causal context and assigns target, past-only-covariate and known-future-covariate roles. On a specified one-day, univariate forecast from 2,048 time steps of history, the paper reports 17–113 ms latency on eight CPU threads. In a separate author-run IND-Eval analysis on 187 industrial forecasting tasks, the paper also reports Timestral-209M leading eleven compared models on two aggregate metrics (0.646 nmase and 0.435 ncrps versus t0-gamma at 0.697 and 0.469). That evaluation is not independent. The model family was announced on October 15, and the models, report and inference code are public. Benchmark and latency results are author-reported; no independent reproduction or realized operating-cost advantage is established.
